Control Description: Block public access to customer data storage, restrict bucket policies, monitor configuration changes, and require documented approval for exceptions.
Test Procedure: Inspect storage public-access settings and bucket policies; attempt to identify unintended public access
Assessor Notes: Design addresses prevention of public exposure through S3 Block Public Access and restrictive bucket policies. Monitoring of configuration changes and documented exception approval are included in the proposed control design. Implementation and operating effectiveness remain unverified.

Control Description: Require encryption at rest for all customer data stored in approved AWS services, including databases, object storage, backups, and snapshots. Enforce encryption through approved configurations and policies, using AWS KMS or an approved encryption mechanism. Restrict key administration and usage through least-privilege IAM and KMS key policies, review key permissions periodically, and configure key rotation in accordance with organizational requirements. Monitor encryption configurations for unauthorized changes or disabled encryption, generate security alerts, and document investigation and remediation activities. Maintain evidence of encryption coverage and periodically validate that customer data remains encrypted at rest.
Test Procedure: Inspect AWS database, object storage, backup, and snapshot encryption configurations to verify that encryption at rest is enabled for all customer data. Review AWS KMS key policies, IAM permissions, key administration restrictions, and key rotation settings. Inspect approved encryption policies and preventive enforcement mechanisms. Review AWS Config rules, CloudTrail events, and CloudWatch alarms for detection of disabled encryption or unauthorized configuration changes. Examine sample alerts, investigation records, remediation tickets, and periodic encryption coverage reviews to verify that encryption requirements are consistently monitored and enforced.
Findings: No implementation evidence has been collected to verify encryption coverage across customer databases, object storage, backups, or snapshots. AWS KMS key policies, IAM permissions, key rotation settings, preventive enforcement mechanisms, and encryption monitoring configurations have not been inspected. Expected evidence E-003, E-004, and E-005 remains simulated and not collected. Implementation has not been verified, and operating effectiveness has not been tested.
Assessor Notes: The revised control design establishes encryption requirements for customer data at rest, including databases, object storage, backups, and snapshots. It specifies encryption enforcement, least-privilege KMS and IAM access, key administration restrictions, key rotation, configuration monitoring, security alerting, investigation, remediation, and periodic validation. These design requirements are considered sufficiently defined for an Adequate design assessment. However, implementation remains unverified because actual organizational configurations and supporting records have not been collected. Expected evidence E-003, E-004, and E-005 is simulated, not verified organizational evidence. Operating effectiveness remains untested.

Control Description: Establish and enforce a formal employee onboarding, offboarding, and role-change access management process. Require prompt deactivation of user accounts and revocation of associated credentials, active sessions, authentication tokens, and privileged access when employees leave the organization. For employees changing roles, review existing permissions and remove access that is no longer required. Coordinate personnel status changes between Human Resources and the IAM Administrator to ensure access modifications occur within documented timeframes. Maintain audit logs of account deactivation and permission changes, and periodically review access management records to verify compliance with organizational security requirements.

Findings: Implementation has not been verified. No actual employee termination records, IAM account deactivation logs, credential revocation records, or role-change access removal records have been collected. Expected evidence E-026 remains simulated and not collected. Operating effectiveness has not been tested.
Assessor Notes: The control design establishes formal onboarding, offboarding, and role-change procedures, including prompt account deactivation, credential and session revocation, HR coordination, and audit logging. However, actual implementation cannot be confirmed because supporting HR and IAM records have not been collected. Evidence E-026 is simulated, not verified organizational evidence. Operating effectiveness remains untested.

Control Description: Establish and enforce periodic reviews of user access permissions across organizational systems, applications, databases, and cloud environments. Require managers and designated system owners to review and approve user access at least quarterly to verify that permissions remain appropriate for assigned job responsibilities. Identify excessive, inappropriate, dormant, or unauthorized permissions and require timely removal or modification. Maintain documented access review records, approval evidence, identified exceptions, and remediation tracking. Perform additional access reviews following significant organizational or employee role changes and periodically evaluate privileged accounts to ensure compliance with access management requirements.

Assessor Notes: The control design establishes periodic access reviews, manager and system owner approvals, least privilege, separation of duties, and remediation tracking. However, actual review performance and approval records cannot be confirmed because supporting IAM and access review documentation has not been collected. Evidence E-025 and E-027 is simulated, not verified organizational evidence. Operating effectiveness remains untested.

Control Description: Establish and enforce network security group configuration standards across cloud infrastructure to restrict inbound and outbound traffic to approved sources, destinations, protocols, and required ports. Apply the principle of least privilege when defining network access rules and prohibit unrestricted public access to sensitive administrative services, including SSH (port 22) and RDP (port 3389), unless explicitly authorized through documented exceptions and appropriate security safeguards. Require approval and documentation for security group rule modifications. Conduct periodic reviews of network access configurations to identify and remove overly permissive, unnecessary, outdated, or unauthorized rules. Maintain configuration records and monitoring evidence to verify continued compliance with organizational network security requirements.
Test Procedure: Inspect cloud security group inbound and outbound rules, verify permitted sources, destinations, protocols, and ports against approved network requirements, and identify unrestricted administrative access such as SSH or RDP from the internet. Review documented approvals for exceptions and network rule changes, and verify periodic reviews identify and remediate unnecessary or overly permissive rules.
Findings: Implementation has not been verified. No actual production security group configurations, inbound rule exports, approved administrative source IP records, or network change approvals have been collected. Expected evidence E-028 and E-029 remains simulated and not collected. Operating effectiveness has not been tested.
Assessor Notes: The control design establishes least-privilege network access restrictions, prohibits unrestricted public exposure of administrative services such as SSH and RDP, requires documented approval of network rule changes, and establishes periodic configuration reviews. However, actual security group configurations and approved network access records have not been collected. Evidence E-028 and E-029 is simulated, not verified organizational evidence. Operating effectiveness remains untested.

Monitor security group rules, network access control lists, routing configurations, public network exposure, and other critical network resources. Implement centralized logging and monitoring using approved security services, including AWS CloudTrail, AWS Config, and Amazon CloudWatch where appropriate. Operating effectiveness remains untested.

Control Description: Establish and enforce a documented backup management process for critical customer databases and business information. Implement automated backups at frequencies determined by business recovery requirements and data criticality. Define and enforce backup retention schedules to ensure recovery points meet organizational requirements. Protect backup copies through approved encryption mechanisms, restricted access permissions, and appropriate safeguards against unauthorized modification or deletion. Where appropriate, maintain immutable, isolated, or cross-account backup copies to reduce exposure to ransomware and infrastructure compromise. Monitor backup operations for failures and investigate unsuccessful backup jobs. Periodically perform restoration tests to verify backup integrity, data availability, and the organization's ability to recover critical information within established recovery objectives. Maintain backup schedules, retention records, monitoring logs, and restoration test results as audit evidence.
Test Procedure: Inspect backup schedules, retention settings, encryption configurations, and access restrictions for critical database backups. Verify backup job monitoring and failure alerts. Review evidence of immutable, isolated, or cross-account backup protection where applicable. Inspect sample backup restoration test results and verify recovery objectives are addressed.
Findings: Implementation and operating effectiveness could not be verified because AWS backup configurations, retention settings, backup protection mechanisms, and database restoration test records have not been collected. E-006, E-007, and E-008 are simulated evidence references rather than verified organizational evidence. No actual backup configuration, retention enforcement, encryption, access restriction, backup monitoring, or successful restoration results were available for review.
Assessor Notes: Control design is adequate. Implementation remains unverified and operating effectiveness remains untested. E-006, E-007, and E-008 identify expected evidence but are currently simulated and not collected. Additional evidence is required, including AWS Backup configuration, backup schedules, retention settings, encryption and access controls, backup job monitoring, and documented database restoration test results.

Control Description: Conduct documented restoration tests for critical systems and data at planned intervals and following significant changes or recovery events. Verify the integrity of backups and restoration assets before use, execute restoration procedures according to documented recovery priorities, and confirm that restored systems and data are accurate, secure, and operational before returning them to service. Record actual restoration time and data recovery results, compare them against approved Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs), and document test results, deficiencies, corrective actions, and retesting.
Test Procedure: Obtain documented restoration test records for selected critical systems. Verify that backup or restoration assets were checked for integrity before use. Review the restoration steps performed and confirm that restored systems and data were checked for integrity, security, and operational functionality before returning to service. Compare actual restoration time and data recovery results with approved RTO and RPO targets. Review test results, documented deficiencies, corrective actions, and evidence of retesting where failures or recovery-target deviations occurred.
Findings: Implementation and operating effectiveness could not be verified because supporting disaster recovery documentation, approved RTO/RPO requirements, and actual restoration test records have not been collected. E-009 and E-010 are simulated evidence references rather than verified organizational evidence. No documented restoration test results, recovery-target comparisons, or corrective-action records were available for review.
Assessor Notes: Control design is adequate. Implementation remains unverified and operating effectiveness remains untested. E-009 and E-010 identify expected evidence but are currently simulated and not collected. Additional evidence is required, including approved disaster recovery procedures, management-approved RTO/RPO targets, documented restoration test results, integrity and operational validation, actual recovery measurements, and corrective-action or retesting records.

Control Description: Identify vulnerabilities affecting production systems through regular vulnerability scanning, security assessments, and review of relevant security advisories. Evaluate identified vulnerabilities based on severity, exploitability, asset criticality, exposure, and potential business impact. Prioritize vulnerabilities according to documented risk criteria, assign remediation ownership, establish remediation deadlines based on risk severity, and track identified vulnerabilities through resolution or formally approved risk acceptance.
Test Procedure: Obtain vulnerability scan results and supporting vulnerability assessment records for selected production systems. Verify that identified vulnerabilities are evaluated using documented risk criteria, including severity, exploitability, asset criticality, and business impact. Confirm that vulnerabilities are prioritized according to risk, assigned to responsible remediation owners, and given remediation deadlines. Review vulnerability tracking records to verify remediation progress, closure evidence, and formal risk acceptance documentation where applicable.
Findings: Implementation has not been verified. Vulnerability scanning configurations, vulnerability assessment records, documented remediation deadlines, and remediation tracking evidence have not been collected. Expected evidence E-011, E-012, and E-013 remains simulated and has not been collected.
Assessor Notes: The control design is adequate because it establishes a risk-based process for identifying, evaluating, prioritizing, assigning, and tracking vulnerabilities. Implementation remains unverified because supporting vulnerability scan reports, approved remediation policies, and remediation tracking records have not been collected. Operating effectiveness has not been tested. Evidence E-011, E-012, and E-013 is simulated expected evidence, not verified organizational evidence.

Control Description: Identify and prioritize security patches for production systems based on vulnerability severity, exploitability, asset criticality, and potential business impact. Evaluate patches for compatibility and operational risk before deployment, and apply approved security patches within documented remediation timeframes based on risk severity. Verify successful patch installation through system configuration reviews and follow-up vulnerability scans. Track outstanding vulnerabilities, failed deployments, and patch exceptions through resolution or formally approved risk acceptance, documenting remediation activities and supporting evidence.
Test Procedure: Obtain patch management records for selected production systems and identify security patches associated with critical vulnerabilities. Verify that patches are prioritized according to documented risk criteria and assigned remediation deadlines. Review patch testing and approval records to confirm compatibility and operational risks were evaluated before deployment. Inspect deployment records and system configuration evidence to verify successful patch installation. Review follow-up vulnerability scan results to confirm identified vulnerabilities were remediated. Examine outstanding vulnerabilities, failed deployments, documented exceptions, and approved risk acceptance records.
Findings: Implementation has not been verified. Patch management configurations, patch deployment records, follow-up vulnerability scan results, and approved remediation exception records have not been collected. Expected evidence E-014 and E-015 remains simulated and has not been collected.
Assessor Notes: The control design is adequate because it establishes a risk-based patch management process covering patch prioritization, compatibility review, deployment, and remediation verification. Implementation remains unverified because patch deployment records, follow-up vulnerability scan results, and approved exception records have not been collected. Operating effectiveness has not been tested. Evidence E-014 and E-015 is simulated expected evidence, not verified organizational evidence.
